{{Short description|Topologies defined on the set of smooth mappings between manifolds}}
In mathematics, and especially [[differential topology]], [[functional analysis]] and [[Singularity theory#Arnold.27s view|singularity theory]], the '''Whitney topologies''' are a [[countably infinite]] family of [[General topology#Definition|topologies]] defined on the set of [[smooth mapping]]s between two [[smooth manifold]]s. They are named after the American mathematician [[Hassler Whitney]].

==Construction==
Let ''M'' and ''N'' be two real, smooth manifolds. Furthermore, let [[Smooth mapping#Multivariate differentiability classes|C<sup>∞</sup>]](''M'',''N'') denote the space of smooth mappings between ''M'' and ''N''. The notation C<sup>∞</sup> means that the mappings are infinitely differentiable, i.e. [[partial derivative]]s of all orders exist and are [[continuous function|continuous]].<ref>{{Citation|first1=M.|last1=Golubitsky|author1-link=Marty Golubitsky|first2=V.|last2=Guillemin|author2-link=Victor Guillemin|title=Stable Mappings and Their Singularities |publisher=Springer|year=1974|ISBN=0-387-90072-1|page=1}}</ref>

===Whitney C<sup>''k''</sup>-topology===
For some [[integer]] {{nowrap|1=''k'' ≥ 0}}, let J<sup>''k''</sup>(''M'',''N'') denote the [[jet (mathematics)|''k''-jet space]] of mappings between ''M'' and ''N''. The jet space can be endowed with a [[smooth structure]] (i.e. a structure as a C<sup>∞</sup> manifold) which make it into a [[topological space]]. This topology is used to define a topology on C<sup>∞</sup>(''M'',''N'').

For a fixed [[integer]] {{nowrap|1=''k'' ≥ 0}} consider an open subset {{nowrap|1=''U'' ⊂ J<sup>''k''</sup>(''M'',''N''),}} and denote by ''S<sup>k</sup>''(''U'') the following:
:<math> S^k(U) = \{ f \in C^{\infty}(M,N) : (J^kf)(M) \subseteq U \} . </math>
The sets ''S<sup>k</sup>''(''U'') form a [[basis (topology)|basis]] for the '''Whitney C<sup>''k''</sup>-topology''' on C<sup>∞</sup>(''M'',''N'').<ref name="GG42">{{harvtxt|Golubitsky|Guillemin|1974}}, p.&nbsp;42.</ref>

===Whitney C<sup>∞</sup>-topology===
For each choice of {{nowrap|1=''k'' &ge; 0}}, the Whitney C<sup>''k''</sup>-topology gives a topology for C<sup>∞</sup>(''M'',''N''); in other words the Whitney C<sup>''k''</sup>-topology tells us which subsets of C<sup>∞</sup>(''M'',''N'') are open sets. Let us denote by W<sup>''k''</sup> the set of open subsets of C<sup>∞</sup>(''M'',''N'') with respect to the Whitney C<sup>''k''</sup>-topology. Then the '''Whitney C<sup>∞</sup>-topology''' is defined to be the topology whose [[basis (topology)|basis]] is given by ''W'', where:<ref name="GG42"/>
:<math> W = \bigcup_{k=0}^{\infty} W^k . </math>

==Dimensionality==
Notice that C<sup>∞</sup>(''M'',''N'') has infinite dimension, whereas J<sup>''k''</sup>(''M'',''N'') has finite dimension. In fact, J<sup>''k''</sup>(''M'',''N'') is a real, finite-dimensional manifold. To see this, let {{nowrap|1=ℝ<sup>''k''</sup>[''x''<sub>1</sub>,...,''x''<sub>''m''</sub>]}} denote the space of [[polynomial]]s, with real coefficients, in ''m'' variables of order at most ''k'' and with zero as the [[constant term]]. This is a real [[vector space]] with dimension
:<math> \dim\left\{\R^k[x_1,\ldots,x_m]\right\} = \sum_{i=1}^k \frac{(m+i-1)!}{(m-1)! \cdot i!} = \left( \frac{(m+k)!}{m!\cdot k!} - 1 \right) . </math>
Writing {{nowrap|1=''a'' = dim{ℝ<sup>''k''</sup>[''x''<sub>1</sub>,...,''x''<sub>''m''</sub>]}}} then, by the standard theory of vector spaces {{nowrap|1=ℝ<sup>''k''</sup>[''x''<sub>1</sub>,...,''x''<sub>''m''</sub>] ≅ ℝ<sup>''a''</sup>,}} and so is a real, finite-dimensional manifold. Next, define:
:<math>B_{m,n}^k = \bigoplus_{i=1}^n \R^k[x_1,\ldots,x_m], \implies \dim\left\{B_{m,n}^k\right\} = n \dim \left\{ A_m^k \right\} = n \left( \frac{(m+k)!}{m!\cdot k!} - 1 \right) . </math>
Using ''b'' to denote the dimension ''B''<sup>''k''</sup><sub>''m'',''n''</sub>, we see that {{nowrap|1=''B''<sup>''k''</sup><sub>''m'',''n''</sub> ≅ ℝ<sup>''b''</sup>}}, and so is a real, finite-dimensional manifold.

In fact, if ''M'' and ''N'' have dimension ''m'' and ''n'' respectively then:<ref>{{harvtxt|Golubitsky|Guillemin|1974}}, p.&nbsp;40.</ref>
:<math> \dim\!\left\{J^k(M,N)\right\} = m + n + \dim \!\left\{B_{n,m}^k\right\} = m + n\left( \frac{(m+k)!}{m!\cdot k!}\right). </math>

==Topology==
Given the Whitney C<sup>∞</sup>-topology, the space C<sup>∞</sup>(''M'',''N'') is a [[Baire space]], i.e. every [[residual set]] is [[dense (topology)|dense]].<ref>{{harvtxt|Golubitsky|Guillemin|1974}}, p.&nbsp;44.</ref>
